question.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.3),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{(0.7)}^{x-1}(0.3), & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 4) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3,4\}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=2)+P(X=3)+P(X=4) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & ={(0.7)}^{0}(0.3)+{(0.7)}^{1}(0.3)+{(0.7)}^{2}(0.3)+{(0.7)}^{3}(0.3) \\  & =0.7599.\end{aligned}
$$
